items.title: Historical operation lifecycles
items.text: Use this page to follow inputs from source evidence to a publication. The operations use different preparation, execution, and recovery contracts.

items.title: Acquisition and source registration
items.text: A data request declares venue, instrument or family scope, feed and nominal interval. ExchangeSource validates that scope and returns archive candidates with stable identity and download provenance. A managed acquisition writes the archive copy and records its hash under the managed raw root. Source registration and import cover manually supplied data. A registered object can still need metadata or a profile before it can be normalized. Acquisition guide · Registration declarations

items.title: Normalization
items.text:
flowchart TB
    R["Recipe or archive selection"] --> P["Forge resolves evidence"]
    P -->|"inputs pinned"| B["Prepared batch v4"]
    P -->|"selection fails"| X["Preparation report"]
    B -->|"batch submission"| E["Engine validates and processes"]
    E -->|"failure"| F["Result and diagnostics"]
    E -->|"validated output"| O["Committed publications"]
    O --> V["Forge verifies inventory"]
    V -->|"verified"| D["Registry publication and files"]

A modern TOML recipe supplies requests and an interval. Forge uses catalogues, rankings where needed, raw archives and historical specification evidence to prepare jobs by content type. Follow batch.py from recipe matching to the schema-4 batch and engine/src/historical/config/batch.rs from structural validation to resolved tasks and profiles. The managed normalizer runs a batch, and Forge checks its structured outcome against the submitted batch. Batch producer · Engine loader

For trade data, follow source decoding, canonical fields, ordering and reconciliation. For depth, follow source observations, initialization, operation semantics, segmentation and canonical level output. Profiles govern fields and interpretation; format readers govern how records get to that interpretation. Committed data includes primary Parquet and manifest-declared auxiliary evidence, plus resolved job and runtime provenance. Forge verifies before registration. Inspect submitted-batch.json, execution-intent.json and execution-result.json under the normalization execution run. Use the documented registration-only recovery for verified committed outputs. A batch can have different outcomes per job. Normalization workflow · Prepared and publication contracts

items.title: Merge
items.text:
flowchart TB
    R["Merge recipe"] --> S["Resolve normalized files"]
    S --> J["Pinned MergeJob"]
    J --> V["Engine job validation"]
    V -->|"accepted"| E["Merge partition execution"]
    V -->|"rejected"| B["Retain generated job and report"]
    E -->|"checks pass"| O["Committed merge"]
    O --> D["Forge verifies and registers"]

A direct selector uses registered normalized file dataset IDs. A derived recipe can follow a normalization recipe through retained evidence and registry membership. Forge resolves complete selected files and pins paths, hashes, identities and ranks into one MergeJob. The merger's --validate-job verifies the submitted contract against the selected inputs without merging. A job that can be serialized but fails validation can remain in the run directory as generated. Merge preparation and execution service · Merge workflow

Rust produces a physical trades, depth or combined timeline. Chronological physical schema 1 and causal physical schema 2 use the manifest's physical-schema and ordering fields. Causal timeline sequence and reconstruction markers carry information the event timestamp alone cannot express. Registry file memberships and publication-level selected dependencies have different scopes. Use the retained merge execution intent for supported registration-only recovery after verifying the committed output. Physical manifest validator · Publication formats

items.title: Conversion
items.text:
flowchart TB
    R["Conversion recipe"] --> P["Verify merge and reference lineage"]
    P --> C["Forge collection"]
    C --> J["Standalone ConvertJob"]
    J --> V["Engine validation"]
    V -->|"run requested and accepted"| E["Materialize and publish"]
    V -->|"incompatible"| B["Retained compatibility evidence"]
    E --> O["Converted manifest and receipt"]

Forge accepts derivation from merge, normalization or acquisition TOML. The selected source still resolves to a complete registered merge publication. Explicit references resolve to trade streams in the source or a supported external trade merge. Reference reachability does not guarantee that an eligible price observation exists before a specific event. Conversion workflow · Conversion configuration

Each current Rust job carries schema version 1, prepared publication identity and fingerprints, stream identities and currencies, catalogue fingerprint, conversion policy, resources and Parquet settings. The Forge convert.json collection indexes separate job files. The Rust CLI consumes one --job, with --validate available to check the job and its evidence before execution. Current execution uses embedded metadata. A fixed on-disk instrument catalogue is not required by the Engine; Forge can check one when it exists during preparation. Old jobs from the pre-standalone contract require regeneration. ConvertJob · Converter entry point

Forge's dry run computes proposed jobs without writing or invoking the Engine. Regular preparation retains a report whose compatibility field records validation separately from generation. Execution submits retained per-job bytes after pin and compatibility checks. The Engine supports causal input through its ordering-aware processing paths. Output has its own conversion manifest and execution receipt. Forge verifies completed output and reports registration as unavailable. A retry from retained preparation requires intact pinned inputs and available output and staging destinations. Conversion orchestration

items.title: Managed historical pipeline
items.text:
flowchart TD
    Scope["Validated pipeline recipe"] --> Plan["Plan and retained run"]
    Plan --> Raw["Acquire and verify raw revisions"]
    Raw --> Batch["Prepare normalization batch"]
    Batch --> Run["Execute and register normalized files"]
    Run --> Merge["Prepare merge from those file IDs"]
    Merge --> Result["Execute and register merge"]
    Batch --> Stop["Optional stop after preparation"]

Resume reads the retained run state and evidence. The preparation stop retains a batch and allows normalization execution to be resumed. Conversion has its own source selection, preparation and executor. Pipeline guide · Retained artifact contracts

items.title: Extend orchestration and persistence
items.text: Use this guide for Forge changes that cross CLI, database, or publication boundaries. Start by identifying the operation owner and the persisted evidence its downstream consumers need.

items.title: Change Forge orchestration
items.text:
A conversion or merge input selector is a representative change. Keep CLI parsing and rendering in the operation's command module. Resolve the workspace and configuration using ApplicationContext, ProjectPaths, and the existing managed configuration library. Send both JSON and terminal requests through the same service so they make the same selection and return consistent exit statuses.

  1. State whether the selector names an instrument, file dataset, registry publication, or Engine publication. Follow the current merge or conversion discovery service for lineage verification and deterministic handling of competing outputs.
  2. Validate editable TOML separately from database-backed preparation. Prepared contracts pin inputs and carry operation-specific fields. Preserve Engine IDs exactly through JSON and registry text representations. Keep dry-run behavior consistent with the operation's current contract. For conversion it writes no artifacts and invokes no Engine.
  3. Reuse the managed binary resolver and supported production validation interface. A built binary and an installed binary can differ. Retain the submitted bytes and ensure the operation verifies the pinned job before launching. Test paths with spaces, explicit paths vs managed names, ambiguity, missing inputs, stale pins, and nonzero exits.
  4. Separate execution, physical validation, and registration in the result. Review the operation's recovery interfaces before adding a suggested recovery command. Update the CLI reference and the relevant workflow and prepared contract.

For a good nearby example, trace merge prepare_job from file selection to --validate-job. Follow test_validation_rejection_keeps_generated_job_and_blocks_processing to see why valid JSON must not become a claim that the Engine can run it. Merge service · Merge CLI integration tests

items.title: Change catalogue or registry behavior
items.text:
Keep provider identity, execution venue and historical specification authority separate. For example, registering an external perpetual recording needs the observed source provenance and a resolved instrument and effective contract specification. A symbol match against the latest instrument catalogue alone cannot prove how to interpret a historical contract quantity. Inspect registration preflight and the normalization preparation path to see where missing or ambiguous evidence stops a request.

Use the existing migration sequence for a schema change. Applied migration scripts are identified and checksum-checked. Add a new migration for a change rather than editing a script already applied. Run it against a clean testing registry and the relevant previous schema in an isolated fixture. Check preserved IDs, rollback on failure and idempotent registration where those guarantees apply. Avoid broad cleanup of shared testing data.

When testing lineage, assert both publication-level dependencies and any exact file-level contribution that the evidence supports. register_files derives records from verified publication evidence and distinguishes file membership scope. Test a stale fingerprint or inconsistent path to establish the rejection boundary. Update the registration reference and dataset CLI if the visible semantics change. Registration preflight · Migration runner · File registration

items.title: Change publications or dataset readers
items.text:
For a new column, manifest field or auxiliary index, trace the producer, content and checksum validation, registration summary, and every reader. For example, causal merge preserves sequence and reconstruction in physical schema 2. Python discovery must verify exact per-file rank membership rather than assuming every rank between the Parquet statistics endpoints is present. Registry summaries can enrich that conclusion only when they agree with physical evidence and their declared scope.

Change Verify Physical column or type Arrow schema, nullability, decimal scale, signed integer nanoseconds, masked or nested values, and mixed-schema behavior Manifest inventory or ownership range Commit-time checks, registered primary paths, checksum coverage, referenced auxiliary content, and rejection of conflicting metadata Dataset preview or scan Field projection, materialization behavior, timestamp filtering, bounded previews and unsupported projection diagnostics Stream membership Multi-stream primary files, evidence for exact ranks, and behavior with missing or inconsistent registry information

Use test_causal_merge.py for small manifest-backed Parquet examples. Use full publication validation when the change affects conclusions drawn from committed output, and test legacy versions still accepted by the consumer. Update the publication formats and Python dataset API at the boundary changed. Discovery · Dataset and stream handles · Causal discovery tests

Read the component chapters for implementation details. Forge · Normalization Engine · Merge Engine · Conversion Engine

items.title: Verify a persisted-field change end to end
items.text:
Use the published depth observation row span as a worked boundary. A fixture with a retained zero-row observation followed by one changed level establishes two different expectations. The first observation remains addressable at its offset with count zero. The next observation has the same starting offset and count one. Encode these expectations from the input when extending the schema.

  1. Change the operation’s writer and its manifest or schema declaration together. Follow normalization output and use the normalized publication reference to identify affected fields.
  2. Update structural and row-span validators before adding a consumer. In merge, inspect replay of a selected part and the mapping from canonical rows to observation spans. In Forge, check how inventory, registry summaries and Stream readers encounter legacy files.
  3. Run the focused historical normalization and merge suites and the Forge dataset reader tests. Check schema nullability, field units, the zero-row event and preservation of physical ordering. Use test selection for commands and prerequisites.
  4. State whether existing artifacts remain readable, then update the publication reference and any affected inspection procedure.

items.title: Performance
items.text: Measure one workload and one processing boundary at a time. Separate correctness, compatibility, wall time, and resource consumption in the results. Start from the application's effective runtime settings and actual input inventory.

items.title: Inspect before benchmarking
items.text:
Use normalization's runtime diagnostics and processing counters to identify phases, tasks, resource admission and integrity observations. Use dataset metadata for rows, row groups and physical bytes. Source compressed bytes, decoded rows, canonical rows and logical events measure different work. A preview limit constrains the returned rows, while Parquet page and batch reads can decode more. Runtime policy · Python dataset API

When comparing an apparent regression, establish whether the difference came from download, source decoding, processing, publish validation or registry work. A timer spanning the entire Forge command includes costs outside the Engine. A profile of one process can miss worker admission, storage or other processes. Keep the measured window explicit.

items.title: Use the normalization benchmark harness
items.text:
The repository contains marketforge-normalize-benchmark. Its CLI accepts an explicit prepared batch, configuration root, worker counts, scheduler, repetitions, warmups, and retention policy. Build the benchmark target in release mode. The example below plans the maintained workload. It requires the referenced inputs, installed profiles and the historical runtime configuration. Planning does not run the trials.

cargo build --locked --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml \
  --release --features historical --bin marketforge-normalize-benchmark
engine/target/release/marketforge-normalize-benchmark \
  --input engine/tests/historical/fixtures/normalize.json --project-root . --dry-run

A real run requires an explicitly supplied workload and authorization under the repository's benchmark guidance. Use an isolated output under data/benchmarks/historical/. Preserve the plan, report and retained diagnostics. The target directory in the command is Cargo's default; use the actual binary location if you override it.

For already collected runs, use the harness's summarize --run PATH and compare --baseline PATH --candidate PATH subcommands. Review the reported comparability before interpreting ratios. The harness records trial status and available process metrics; inspect missing metrics, failed trials and warmups before aggregating. Benchmark argument model · Benchmark runner

items.title: Record enough context to reproduce a comparison
items.text:
Record Why it matters Revision, build profile, features and executable checksum Debug/release or feature differences can dominate one code change Input fixture and fingerprints, content type, bytes, tasks and logical events Workload changes can change both cost and correctness Effective workers, memory, scratch, file/row-group targets and scheduler Requested settings can be constrained by actual admission and runtime configuration Machine, storage, OS, cache conditions and competing load CPU, physical IO and page cache affect repeated runs Time window, repetition order, warmups and failures A single fastest run, censored timeout or mixed set of phases can mislead Correctness check and expected output A faster execution can result from omitted work or changed semantics

Separate measured RSS from Engine-accounted memory. Treat missing process metrics as unknown. Compare event or row counts and independently understand any intentional output difference before accepting a throughput claim. The historical verifier includes synthetic and dry-run benchmark contract tests. Those tests establish harness behavior. Record the input, executable revision, and resource settings alongside any measured result.

items.title: Local development
items.text: Set up a checkout and verify the Python and Rust toolchains before using providers or the testing registry. All commands here start at the repository root unless shown in a subshell.

items.title: Install the toolchains
items.text:
On Linux or macOS, install the contributor environment and select it for the uv run commands below:

./install.sh --dev --skip-market-init
export UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT="$PWD/.install/dev"

For manual setup, use Python 3.12 or newer, uv, Neovim, and Rust/Cargo 1.89 or newer. The repository has no checked-in Rust toolchain pin or declared Cargo minimum Rust version. Cargo.lock pins dependencies. Managed Engine builds target the host and reject a configured foreign target. Conversion's atomic no-replace publication implementation is Linux-only.

uv sync --project forge --locked --group dev --group lab
uv run --project forge --locked mf --version
rustc --version
cargo --version

uv uses the Forge project environment, normally forge/.venv. The dev group includes pytest, Ruff and Pyright. The lab group includes PyArrow, Polars, JupyterLab, and ipykernel. Keep --group lab on commands that exercise dataset inspection or its tests. Forge installs the mf and marketforge entry points from the same package. Use uv run --project forge … from the checkout to select that environment explicitly. Configuration and paths derive from the checkout or the global --project-root argument. Python project configuration · Cargo features and targets

items.title: Check a small baseline
items.text:
uv run --project forge --locked --group dev pytest -c forge/pyproject.toml \
  forge/tests/unit/historical/archives/test_source_regressions.py -k observed_bybit_directory_variants
cargo test --locked --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml \
  --features historical --test historical_normalize depth_boundary::

The Python selection exercises three saved Bybit listing variants through an HTTP mock. The Rust selection covers depth boundary checks. Each command should report tests passing with a nonzero number selected. Neither requires provider access nor a registry. Cargo typically uses engine/target and may download locked dependencies on the first build. See Testing for wider selections and fixture prerequisites.

items.title: Build the executable Forge will use
items.text:
uv run --project forge --locked mf engine build normalize --dry-run
uv run --project forge --locked mf engine build normalize
uv run --project forge --locked mf engine status

Use merge or convert as the explicit target when that stage changes. The default managed build selects normalization. Forge builds approved release targets with the historical and monitor features and installs independent copies under .bin/. Cargo's own build output is separate. A direct Cargo test or build leaves Forge's installed executable as it was. engine status reports the installed checksum and recorded revision. Compare that revision to the code you intend to exercise, and rebuild after relevant edits. A verified checksum establishes installation integrity. Recorded revision and dirty state are limited source provenance. Managed Engine implementation · Engine CLI

items.title: Set up the testing registry when needed
items.text:
Follow installation and database setup to create a PostgreSQL database named marketforge_test and configure its role. Use a nonblank TEST_DATABASE_KEY or the same key in the checkout's .secrets/postgres.env. Forge reads that file as data. Keep the URL out of commands, reports, and Git.

uv run --project forge --locked mf database migrate --testing
uv run --project forge --locked mf database status --testing

Migration writes to the selected database. Verify purpose testing and review pending migrations in the status output. Testing workflows check both the database name and the purpose marker. Some pytest fixtures require the environment variable explicitly even when a CLI would use the file. See Testing database for fixture behavior. Schema setup needs no provider metadata download. Use the separate Bybit Quick Start when you intend to populate market metadata and acquire archives.

items.title: Verify installer changes
items.text:
The installer tests use mocked package managers by default. Run them with the Forge development environment from the checkout:

uv run --project forge --locked --group dev pytest scripts/install/tests

To include the PostgreSQL test, set MARKETFORGE_INSTALL_TEST_PG_BIN to the directory containing initdb, pg_ctl, and psql. The test starts its own temporary cluster and uses separate databases. It requires a non-root user.

items.title: Build and preview the handbook
items.text:
Zensical is pinned in docs/requirements.txt. The development installer makes it available in .install/docs:

(cd docs && ../.install/docs/bin/zensical build --strict)
python3 docs/check_links.py

For a manual installation, use a separate documentation environment.

python3 -m venv docs/.venv
docs/.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
(cd docs && .venv/bin/zensical build --strict)
python3 docs/check_links.py
(cd docs && .venv/bin/zensical serve)

The build writes to ignored docs/site/. Stop the preview with Ctrl-C. Inspect navigation, links and diagrams in the browser. The native Mermaid fence added in docs/zensical.toml lets Zensical initialize rendering on pages with diagrams. A Markdown build verifies page generation. A browser check verifies Mermaid rendering. The pinned Zensical theme fetches the Mermaid runtime when a diagram page loads. Zensical diagrams

The commands in this handbook work without a clipboard helper. If your shell has cpout, use it separately for human-readable output. In Bash or Zsh, enable set -o pipefail before piping a check so the check's failure reaches the shell. Keep interactive commands and machine-consumed output in their original form.

items.title: Extend source integration and processing
items.text: Use this guide to place a source change at the correct boundary. The examples follow Bybit BTC perpetual data from provider discovery to canonical trades and depth. Run focused tests in the local environment and keep a small raw sample with a known outcome when changing interpretation.

items.title: Change acquisition discovery
items.text:
Use this path when the provider changes its listing, URI, authentication, pagination, feed variants, or archive download behavior. Acquisition owns locating and identifying objects and recording their nominal time bounds. It does not turn provider records into canonical events.

  1. Start at ArchiveRequest, the internal ArchiveSource protocol, and ExchangeSource.validate and discover. In the Bybit branch, check native scope requirements and the final response URL before parsing a listing. Mirror that dispatch and validation for new provider behavior. Adding a provider also requires checking how the calling acquisition service constructs its source and how the venue or provider authority is registered.
  2. Build a DiscoveredArchive with the correct source request, source object key, filename and nominal half-open interval. Use the provider's calendar or archive semantics for time bounds. archive_scope_document and archive_scope_key are part of the storage identity. Feed variants can share a symbol and date while requiring distinct identities.
  3. Keep temporary or signed URLs separate from stable object identity. Distinguish a successful empty listing from an error page or incomplete collection. Validate access, redirects, returned scope, and malformed links before handing a candidate to download or cache logic.
  4. Check the persistence path through archive registry and managed acquisition storage. Preserve the local archive hash, source object relationship, storage root and relative path. An external file can enter through the registration/import path when its bytes and identity are already known.

Use the sanitized Bybit directory examples as the nearby fixture. For a listing change, verify an exact scope, interval, and object key for a positive case. Add a negative page or link that would silently contaminate scope if accepted. If downloads change, also check retention, status and checksums with the relevant storage tests. Update the acquisition configuration, historical acquisition guide, and external data guide when their respective contracts change. Archive source protocol · Provider dispatch · Archive identity

items.title: Change a format profile
items.text:
Use a profile when the representation is already supported and the change can be described with existing field, format, timestamp, quantity and operation mappings. Start with the installed profile for the same venue, instrument type, market category and content type. See the profile authoring workflow, its trade and depth examples, and the authoritative profile reference.

  1. Identify the archive member and raw field shape from a representative sample. State the exact expected canonical timestamp and quantity first. Specify timestamp units and distinguish source event time from system time when the source provides both. For derivative sizes, identify whether the source quantity represents base, quote, or contracts, and verify that effective instrument specifications support the interpretation.
  2. Edit the profile under the identity convention exchange.instrument_type.market_category.data_type. The lifecycle in Forge's profile service inspects and validates TOML and manages installation. Rust's FormatCatalog loads schema-2 catalogue profiles, validates physical and semantic fields and checks the compiled profile against a task. The task and manifest record provenance that downstream checks can use.

  3. Exercise both compiler validation and execution. With a current managed normalizer and installed profiles, run the schema and catalogue check on the Bybit linear perpetual trade profile from the checkout root.

    uv run --project forge --locked mf normalize profiles validate bybit.perpetual.linear.trades

    For a candidate file, use validate --file PATH in place of the installed ID. Forge builds a temporary catalogue containing the candidate and runs the normalizer's production profile validation. This check makes no registry changes.

    A valid profile establishes that the declared format and mappings fit the supported contract. Run a bounded sample to verify the canonical values and any integrity counters. For depth, test one initialization followed by a change and verify the resulting levels and the event index, including an observation that emits no levels if it is relevant. 4. Update the corresponding profile reference only if the contract has changed. Update workflow examples when their supported parameters or expected interpretation change. Keep historical provenance traceable when a same-name profile changes.

Forge profile lifecycle · Rust profile compiler · Profile regression target

items.title: Change a reader or Engine semantics
items.text:
A reader change belongs where bytes become records. Begin with SourceFormat classification and with_source_reader in the normalization worker, then follow trade or depth worker dispatch to the shared format implementation. For a new physical format, audit both ordinary and family-task paths in addition to profile validation. Archive compression and member selection precede record interpretation. A provider download adapter alone cannot add a record encoding.

For a semantic change, start at the worker's downstream boundary. Trade interpretation and reconciliation have different state from a depth book. Depth distinguishes initialization, changes, observations, segments, fingerprints and level rows. Decide whether a rule affects source interpretation, ordering, reconstruction or the persisted format. Check the compatibility impact at the stage where the rule first changes the meaning of an input or output.

Example Expected behavior to write down before coding Source CSV timestamp at a sub-millisecond boundary Exact nanosecond value under the declared timestamp unit, including the null or invalid-field behavior Snapshot then an absolute-size update Resulting size at the affected level, unchanged levels, and the recorded boundary and canonical row offset New decoder record over its configured limit Explicit error through the worker path with bounded input handling Causal timeline consumption Preserved sequence order and reconstruction context even when event timestamps regress

Use the nearby CSV depth pipeline test or a trade fixture to exercise format dispatch. When changing a codec or column reader, exercise invalid bytes, missing fields or members and relevant resource limits. When changing Engine semantics, assert exact values and independently specified state. Add parallel or batch-boundary equivalence coverage where the changed guarantee spans those boundaries. Check merge and conversion consumers if the change touches chronology, provenance fields, event offsets or depth initialization. Worker code · Family processing · Depth CSV pipeline tests · Runtime and integrity policy

items.title: Walkthrough: accept a revised Bybit directory listing
items.text:
Suppose Bybit changes the markup around an existing BTCUSDT archive link while keeping the URL path and filename convention. The owning boundary is listing discovery, since the archive bytes and profile semantics are unchanged.

  1. Open forge/historical/archives/sources/exchanges.py in nvim. Trace the existing Bybit dispatch from ExchangeSource.discover to the directory parser. Add support in that branch so all callers use the same adapter and registry integration.
  2. Start with forge/tests/unit/historical/archives/fixtures/bybit_linear.html. Keep its /trading/BTCUSDT directory and one in-window link such as BTCUSDT2026-11-02.csv.gz. Change the markup to the new form. Add an out-of-window link or a neighboring instrument to test isolation.
  3. Test via the existing httpx.MockTransport harness in test_source_regressions.py. Assert the exact filename, unchanged stable object identity, and nominal interval from November 2 at 00:00 UTC to November 3 at 00:00 UTC for the in-window archive. Check separately that a wrong-instrument-only page produces the existing discovery error and does not masquerade as a successful empty listing.

  4. Run the fixture and negative cases together:

    uv run --project forge --group dev pytest -q \
  forge/tests/unit/historical/archives/test_source_regressions.py -k bybit

  5. If object identity or interval semantics change, review adapter versioning and the discovery-cache and managed-copy tests before accepting the change. A markup-only change keeps the registration shape. Document any new selector in the acquisition recipe reference and any changed operator behavior in the acquisition guide.

The same fixture strategy works for altered pagination or feed variants. Keep the provider boundary assertions about identity and interval separate from profile and Engine assertions about decoded events.

items.title: Testing
items.text:
Choose the smallest test that crosses the boundary you changed. Commands on this page start at the checkout root unless noted.

Change Focused starting point What it establishes Provider requests and archive discovery forge/tests/unit/historical/archives/test_source_regressions.py Scope, intervals and rejection of malformed listings with controlled HTTP responses Forge CLI, job preparation and managed installation forge/tests/integration/cli/test_config.py, forge/tests/integration/cli/test_merge.py, forge/tests/unit/historical/{conversion,engine}/ Command behavior, artifact retention and handoff structure under test-controlled inputs Profile interpretation and historical normalization Cargo target historical_normalize, filter profiles:: or the relevant worker test The parser, compiler or processing behavior selected by the test Exact depth boundaries and source order Cargo target historical_normalize, filter depth_boundary::, plus relevant CSV/depth tests Boundary state and fingerprint semantics. Decode and replay tests exercise additional invariants Merge or conversion validation and persistence Cargo targets historical_merge and historical_convert Engine behavior under generated or explicitly selected committed inputs Registry lineage, migrations, and cross-language execution forge/tests/integration/forge_workflow/test_workflow.py The selected real Forge/Rust/PostgreSQL scenario with fixture-owned schemas Python publication discovery and readers forge/tests/unit/datasets/ Manifest handling, provenance conflicts, timestamp and decimal fidelity, and selected-file inspection Documentation Strict Zensical build, link checker and browser preview Site generation, available targets and rendered diagrams

Inspect the selected test and its fixture before relying on it. A mocked Engine invocation can establish a CLI preflight branch. A real loader test can establish input acceptance. A committed publication assertion can establish the publication behavior it observes. Exact value and state assertions are still needed to prove data semantics.

items.title: Focused commands
items.text:
Use the environments in Local development. Python tests use the pytest configuration in forge/pyproject.toml. The lab group provides Arrow and Polars for dataset tests. The selected tests below use fixtures or mocks and require no external service. Three optional conversion cases skip unless you supply a fresh converter.

uv run --project forge --locked --group dev --group lab pytest -c forge/pyproject.toml \
  forge/tests/unit/historical/archives/test_source_regressions.py \
  forge/tests/unit/datasets forge/tests/unit/historical/conversion \
  forge/tests/integration/cli/test_config.py forge/tests/integration/cli/test_merge.py

To exercise the real converter with Forge-generated jobs and synthetic merge input, build the debug binary and opt in explicitly. These tests use temporary directories and substitute fixture discovery, so they exercise the process handoff and committed output without a database.

cargo build --locked --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --features historical --bin marketforge-convert
MARKETFORGE_TEST_CONVERT_BINARY="$PWD/engine/target/debug/marketforge-convert" \
  uv run --project forge --locked --group dev --group lab pytest -c forge/pyproject.toml \
  forge/tests/unit/historical/conversion/test_conversion.py -k forge_prepared_job_runs_in_real_engine

Use pytest -k to filter names or give an exact path::test_name. Check the test count, skips, and exit status. For a changed Python source, run the configured Ruff linter and formatter and strict Pyright on the affected paths. For example:

uv run --project forge --locked --group dev ruff check forge/historical/archives/sources
uv run --project forge --locked --group dev ruff format --check forge/historical/archives/sources
uv run --project forge --locked --group dev pyright -p forge/pyproject.toml forge/historical/archives/sources

Pyright's configuration targets Python 3.12 and names the repository-root .venv. If your project environment lives elsewhere, use Pyright's --pythonpath to point to that environment's interpreter, such as forge/.venv/bin/python.

For a Rust change, enable the feature gate of the affected target. These examples compile the requested features and run only the named test selection. Test-generated files use the fixture's temporary or retained output directories.

cargo fmt --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
cargo check --locked --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --features historical
cargo test --locked --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --features historical \
  --test historical_normalize depth_boundary::
cargo test --locked --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --features historical \
  --test historical_merge merge_depth_stream::
cargo test --locked --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --features historical \
  --test historical_convert portable::validation_cli_checks_inventory_and_planning_without_writing -- --exact

Cargo's name filter can select zero tests and still exit successfully. Confirm that the intended case ran. For a wider portable check, feature matrix, Clippy target selection, and per-case deadline tooling, start with the bounded Rust verification guide. Run feature configurations in sequence when they share a Cargo target directory. Engine CLI harnesses can launch the binary at Cargo's stable path. The per-case supervisor lists unless passed --run and fails an empty runnable selection.

There is no checked-in CI workflow defining an additional required matrix in this checkout. Repository guidance calls for the applicable formatting, lint/type, and focused verification checks. Run opt-in network or recorded workloads deliberately. A marker or feature gate alone does not imply that an ignored case will run.

items.title: Testing database and artifacts
items.text:
The guarded CLI and shared fixture resolver use TEST_DATABASE_KEY first and can fall back to the same key in .secrets/postgres.env. The connection checks for marketforge_test and the testing purpose marker. Some pytest integration fixtures explicitly skip without the environment variable. Follow the testing registry setup and inspect the selected fixture before running it. These operations can write real files and database records.

The Forge workflow fixture additionally requires MARKETFORGE_FORGE_INTEGRATION=1, a managed normalizer, historical runtime settings and profiles, and a testing role with schema creation privileges. It redirects catalogue, historical and ranking SQL to randomly named schemas, applies migrations there, and drops those schemas on fixture cleanup. Its ordinary cases use pytest temporary roots. The optional Databento BYOD case has external JSONL prerequisites and retains isolated output under data/tests/historical/normalize/. Other integration fixtures have their own cleanup scope. Workflow fixture and tests · BYOD example

To run the synthetic trade/depth workflow case after setting up the guarded registry and normalizer:

MARKETFORGE_FORGE_INTEGRATION=1 uv run --project forge --locked --group dev --group lab \
  pytest -c forge/pyproject.toml \
  forge/tests/integration/forge_workflow/test_workflow.py::test_trade_depth_registration_prepare_edit_execute_retry

Inspect skips and prerequisite failures separately from assertions. Use recorded Engine smoke selections only when the required archives or committed publications are available. Normalization uses feature gates including historical-real-tests and historical-full-tests. The recorded conversion target has a bounded prefix test and a separately ignored full publication case. Relocation variables in the verifier guide are for exact copies of the documented inputs.

items.title: Write and maintain meaningful fixtures
items.text:
A depth snapshot opens a book at a known state. Suppose it contains bid 100 with quantity 2 and ask 101 with quantity 3. An absolute update to the bid at 100 with quantity 1 should leave bid 100 at quantity 1 and the ask unchanged. If the applicable source operation interprets a zero as removal, a subsequent bid update to zero should remove that bid. This is a synthetic oracle. State which source rule applies, then assert the levels, boundary type, and event offsets or zero-row observation expected from the test. Checking only a total row count could miss a side swap or a failure to remove a level.

Fixture family Maintenance Forge provider listings Keep sanitized responses next to the tests in forge/tests/unit/historical/archives/fixtures/. Reproduce relevant URI and calendar evidence with a mock transport. Preserve positive and negative cases and omit private credentials or signed links. Synthetic Rust records and publications Use the nearby support builders or temporary fixtures in engine/tests/historical/. Express expected values independently and retain the reason for unusual timestamps, decimals, sequences or boundaries. Python inspection docs/content/examples/notebooks/dataset_fixtures.py constructs small Parquet and manifest examples. Temporary tests verify discovery and exact values without a registry. Recorded historical workloads The maintained normalization batch is engine/tests/historical/fixtures/normalize.json. The merge fixture is alongside it. Conversion also has committed job fixtures under engine/tests/historical/convert/fixtures/jobs/. The documents identify dependencies. Large raw and publication bytes are separate local inputs. Generated output Keep recordings and generated data outside Git. Use a fresh output root for each run and preserve persistent historical regression evidence. Derive new expectations from source records and the contract before updating snapshots, counts or hashes.

Missing recorded input is a prerequisite failure or an explicit skip under the suite's configured rules. A fixture change should explain why its previous expectation changed and which consumer or invariant it exercises. Historical verifier · Notebook fixture builder

items.title: Conversion verification
items.text:
The portable conversion suite generates small causal publications and exercises the production binary. The test below builds a complete output without database or provider access.

cargo test --locked --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --features historical \
  --test historical_convert

The optional recorded check requires the exact pinned Bybit publication. A relocated copy can be selected with MARKETFORGE_RECORDED_CONVERT_INPUT. The prefix case materializes 4,096 events, including causal reconstruction and reference prehistory. The ignored publishes_canonical_recorded_conversion test is the full recorded replay and requires space for the converted publication.

cargo test --locked --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --features historical-real-tests \
  --test historical_recorded_convert validates_canonical_recorded_prefix_with_causal_prehistory \
  -- --exact --nocapture

items.title: Examples
items.text:
• Bybit BTCUSDT perpetual trades and depth uses the two-request recipe and the installed venue profiles.
  • Synthetic exchange and recordings provide a complete local trade and depth example with fictional specifications.
  • Databento AAPL explains how to register XNAS.ITCH JSONL trades and MBP-10 observations.
  • Merge a compatible trade file uses the verified synthetic trade registration.
  • Convert a synthetic causal publication with the maintained 12-row fixture. The recorded Bybit conversion uses a specific registered publication.

items.title: Bring your own historical data
items.text:
Use managed registration for purchased files, recordings, or exports you already have. Exchange acquisition locates and downloads archives from configured venues. Registration copies the files you select into managed raw storage and records their provenance and interpretation in the same PostgreSQL registry.

  1. Inspect representative source records, including unusual trade sides, missing values, and depth messages at the beginning and end. Confirm timestamp encoding, quantity denomination, instrument identifiers, ordering guarantees, and whether a depth message represents a state or a change. Use provider documentation to establish sequence semantics.
  2. Declare the venue, instrument, and time-bounded specifications through mf catalog. For equities use the equity.equity instrument/category pair, the ticker as the base asset, the currency as quote asset, and base quantity for shares. Supply applicable price and quantity increments with provenance. See the catalogue setup.
  3. Author a self-contained schema-2 TOML profile. Match its filename and ID to venue.instrument_type.market_category.trades or venue.instrument_type.market_category.depth. Declare the physical format in [source], the raw fields in [fields.*], and explicit transformations in [normalization]. Use mf normalize profiles validate --file PATH for Rust semantic validation, then mf normalize profiles add ID --from PATH --testing to install it. One layout can be installed per profile ID, subject to the existing Gate.io feed variants. See the profile authoring reference.
  4. Write a registration TOML with provider, product, source key, provenance, root, coverage, and file selections. Each input pairs a concrete catalogue instrument with an installed profile. The root is relative to the project root unless absolute. Use mf acquisition register plan PATH --testing to check resolved bindings, then mf acquisition register run PATH --testing to checksum and copy files. Repeat registration can reuse verified files.
  5. Write a normalization recipe selecting the registered source key, venue, instrument, data type, and interval. Run mf --json normalize prepare PATH --testing. Forge uses PostgreSQL to select managed copies and resolve instrument and specification authority, then validates the prepared batch with Rust. Use mf normalize run BATCH.json --testing to execute it. The result maps the primary files to PostgreSQL file dataset IDs and reports the shared publication.
  6. Inspect each dataset's manifest.json and the Parquet paths listed there. Compare physical records read and processed, logical events, canonical rows, exclusions, and integrity counters. For depth, use events.parquet to associate each observation with its canonical row range, including zero-row observations. Check the boundary coverage before interpreting reconstructed state.

Use an export to supported CSV or JSONL when your original format has no reader. Preserve the originals and record the conversion and format in provenance. Native DBN is outside the current normalization workflow. The managed registration and publication commands currently require the configured testing PostgreSQL database.

The Databento AAPL walkthrough includes complete declarations, profiles, and a recipe for both trades and bounded order-book observations.

items.title: Databento AAPL Trades and MBP-10
items.text:
This recording covers AAPL on Nasdaq (xnas) from 14:30 to 14:40 UTC on October 28, 2024. The registry stores Databento as provider and XNAS.ITCH as product. AAPL is a USD equity with quantities in shares. Publisher 2 and native instrument 38 identify the raw observations. PostgreSQL supplies the canonical instrument ID. XNAS.ITCH dataset documentation

  • AAPL_trades.jsonl contains 1,977 executions. The trade profile maps A to sell, B to buy, and N to unknown. It preserves execution prices including sub-cent values and both event and receive timestamps to nanoseconds. Databento Trades
  • AAPL_orderbook_L2.jsonl contains 39,605 MBP-10 messages. The depth profile maps both sides and order counts from levels[]. Each message describes the supplied top ten levels per side. flags & 128 marks the last record of an event for the instrument. Preserve intermediate observations in source order. The raw action and flags remain available in the managed source file. Databento MBP-10 · Databento flags and sides
  • The two .dbn.zst files contain the original Zstandard-compressed DBN binary records. Use the supplied JSONL exports for this workflow. Native DBN decoding is unsupported. Databento Binary Encoding

items.title: Obtain the exports
items.text: Use existing exports or request trades and mbp-10 for AAPL from XNAS.ITCH, with start 2024-10-28T14:30:00Z and exclusive end 2024-10-28T14:40:00Z. The checkout's research/marketforge_databento_equities.ipynb estimates cost, calls the Historical API, and exports the records with the Databento SDK's to_json method. Review the estimate before running the download cell. Place the resulting AAPL_trades.jsonl and AAPL_orderbook_L2.jsonl under .recordings/ in the checkout. The site does not distribute the licensed recordings.

items.title: Inspect and register
items.text:
Run from the project root with Forge installed and a configured testing database. The registration recipe selects the original JSONL filenames under .recordings. The specification illustrates the declaration schema. Replace its illustrative economic parameters and provenance with evidence applicable to the full recording interval before registration. The observed price grid alone does not establish historical venue rules.

examples="$PWD/docs/content/examples/bring-your-own-data/databento"
wc -l .recordings/AAPL_{trades,orderbook_L2}.jsonl
head -n 1 .recordings/AAPL_trades.jsonl | python -m json.tool
head -n 1 .recordings/AAPL_orderbook_L2.jsonl | python -m json.tool

mf database migrate --testing
mf engine build normalize
mf catalog exchange add --from "$examples/exchange.toml" --testing
mf catalog instrument add --from "$examples/instrument.toml" --testing
mf catalog specs add --from verified-aapl-specs.toml --testing
for kind in trades depth; do
    profile="xnas.equity.equity.$kind"
    mf normalize profiles validate --file "$examples/$profile.toml"
    mf normalize profiles add "$profile" --from "$examples/$profile.toml" --testing
done
mf acquisition register plan "$examples/registration.toml" --testing
mf acquisition register run "$examples/registration.toml" --testing

items.title: Prepare and publish
items.text:
The normalization recipe selects the registered source and requests one job per canonical data type. Only the standalone trade file feeds the trade job. The MBP-10 trade messages contribute book observations to the depth job. Their event time, native instrument ID, sequence, price, size, and side match the standalone trades as a multiset.

mf --json normalize run "$examples/normalization.toml" --testing > byod-result.json

items.title: Inspect the output
items.text:
The run report maps each primary Parquet file to its PostgreSQL ID under catalogue_dataset_ids. Inspect file-local row counts, timestamps and membership with:

mf datasets list --testing --exchange xnas --instrument AAPL
mf datasets show FILE_ID --testing
mf datasets head FILE_ID --testing --limit 10

The depth publication retains its indexed observation and boundary metadata in the shared manifest. The observed envelope alone does not establish sequence continuity.

To rerun the full verification against every raw trade and reconstructed depth state, including the overlap check, use the test below. It uses disposable schemas in the testing database and retains isolated artifacts under data/tests/historical/normalize/.

MARKETFORGE_FORGE_INTEGRATION=1 python -m pytest \
  forge/tests/integration/forge_workflow/test_workflow.py -k databento

items.title: Synthetic trade and depth recordings
items.text: This bundle uses a fictional exchange and AAPL specifications. The inputs are one CSV trade and two JSONL book events. The authoring guide explains their mappings.

items.title: Check the emitted records
items.text:
Use a fresh testing workspace and registry setup with the managed normalizer. Run from the checkout where the files below are available. Set up the venue, instrument, and specifications, then install the validated profiles. To check a draft, use its path in the matching iteration of the loop.

example=docs/content/examples/catalogue
for entity in exchange instrument specs; do
    mf catalog "$entity" add --from "$example/$entity.toml" --testing | cpout
done
for kind in trades depth; do
    id="example_exchange.equity.equity.$kind"
    profile="$example/$id.toml"
    if [ "$kind" = depth ]; then profile="$example/incremental/$id.toml"; fi
    mf normalize profiles add "$id" --from "$profile" --testing | cpout
done
mf acquisition register plan "$example/incremental/registration.toml" --testing | cpout
mf acquisition register run "$example/incremental/registration.toml" --testing | cpout
mf --json normalize run "$example/normalization.toml" --testing | cpout

The JSON result gives the registered primary file IDs. Substitute each ID for FILE_ID to preview the records.

mf datasets head FILE_ID --limit 10 --wide --precise --testing | cpout

The trade preview should show a buy of 10 shares at 233.62 and event time 1730125800000000000 ns. The depth snapshot at that timestamp has a bid of 10 at 233.61 and an ask of 12 at 233.63. Apply the next event’s absolute changes to get bid 233.61 × 4 and ask 233.64 × 8, with the old ask removed. Check the dataset inspection guide for other ways to examine the publication.

items.title: Merge a compatible trade file
items.text:
Complete the synthetic normalization example first and install the current managed merger with mf engine build merge. Run from the checkout in the same guarded registry. The example selects the single trade file and a one-nanosecond interval containing its execution. Check the layout restrictions before adapting the recipe to other files.

python - <<'PY'
import json
from pathlib import Path

result = json.loads(Path("synthetic-result.json").read_text())
assert result["status"] == "complete"
for job in result["jobs"]:
    manifest = json.loads(Path(job["manifest_path"]).read_text())
    if manifest["content_type"] == "trades":
        (file_id,) = job["files"].values()
        break
else:
    raise SystemExit("Missing synthetic trade publication.")

with Path("synthetic-merge.toml").open("x") as recipe:
    recipe.write(
        f"dataset_ids = [{file_id}]\n"
        "start_ns = 1730125800000000000\n"
        "end_ns = 1730125800000000001\n"
    )
PY
mf merge validate ./synthetic-merge.toml
mf merge prepare ./synthetic-merge.toml --testing
mf --json merge run ./synthetic-merge.toml --testing > synthetic-merge-result.json
python - <<'PY'
import json
with open("synthetic-merge-result.json") as f:
    result = json.load(f)
assert result["status"] == "complete", result.get("error")
print(*result["catalogue_dataset_ids"].values(), sep="\n")
PY

The checked run registered one output file. Use the printed ID with mf datasets head ID --testing and compare the trade with the original CSV. Run mf datasets lineage ID --testing --publication to see the selected input. The example creates the recipe exclusively. To use it again, review the existing recipe and reuse it if its file ID is still correct.

If prepare reports a job parse error after a code update, rebuild the managed merger and retry preparation. If the engine reports no active stream, check the selected interval and stream coverage. The example's bounds contain exactly the supplied trade timestamp.

items.title: Getting started
items.text:
Use this route to produce a first historical dataset from a fresh checkout.

  1. Install Forge and prepare the workspace. Verify the managed normalizer, the testing registry, and Arrow inspection tools.
  2. Acquire and normalize a day of Bybit BTCUSDT trades and depth. Follow the returned file IDs to inspect the registered output and reconstruct the first book state.
  3. Choose a guide for another market, your own recording, a merge, or a downstream dataset reader.

If your workspace already has a publication, go directly to dataset inspection. For a development checkout or implementation change, start with the developer overview.

items.title: Standard installation
items.text:
On Ubuntu, Debian, or a Homebrew-supported macOS release, clone the repository and run:

git clone https://github.com/flowdrivenml/marketforge.git
cd marketforge
./install.sh

The installer supports x86-64 and ARM64. Run it as your regular user. Ubuntu and Debian may request sudo for packages or local PostgreSQL administration. On macOS, finish the Apple command-line tools installation and rerun if prompted. The installer asks before bootstrapping Homebrew. It does not run Homebrew as root.

The installer verifies or installs Neovim, Python 3.12 or newer, uv, and Rust/Cargo. The current locked Engine requires Rust 1.89 or newer. It synchronizes Forge in .install/runtime and builds and checksums the managed normalize, merge, and convert binaries through Forge. The installer creates a new Forge configuration with presentation.editor = "nvim" when there is no existing configuration. Existing editor settings, Neovim configuration, and plugins are preserved. Conversion’s atomic publication step currently requires Linux.

It installs the mf and marketforge entry points under ~/.local/bin. If they are missing from your PATH, add that directory using your shell’s setup or run ~/.local/bin/mf directly. An occupied launcher path is reported and left alone. Run workspace commands from the checkout or pass --project-root PATH before the command.

items.title: Development installation
items.text:
./install.sh --dev

Development selects the testing database for provisioning, migrations, and initialization. It verifies the runtime tools and adds the locked dev and lab groups, including pytest, pytest-asyncio, Ruff, Pyright, Polars, Arrow, JupyterLab, and ipykernel. It also checks Rustfmt and Clippy and installs the pinned Zensical requirement in .install/docs. The contributor environment is .install/dev. The two environments coexist and working launchers from this checkout are reused. Use the contributor setup for environment selection and test commands.

Forge itself still defaults to production. Use mf tui --testing and pass --testing for testing registry commands.

items.title: Installer options and results
items.text:
Option Behavior --dev Install development tools and select testing. --dry-run Inspect the platform and available executables, then print planned stages without making changes. --skip-postgres Skip PostgreSQL packages, services, and provisioning. Require an explicit connection and still apply the selected migrations. --skip-market-init Finish local setup and database migrations without collecting provider metadata or building rankings. --help Show usage.

On success, the installer exits with status 0. Market initialization is a separate stage after local setup and database verification. It can contact providers to collect market metadata, enrich historical evidence, and publish rankings. A partial or failed initialization exits with status 3 and retains the completed setup. Retry with mf init --production or mf init --testing for the selected registry. Cancellation is reported separately. A failed required installation stage exits with status 1.

Reruns reuse compatible tools, verified binaries, credentials, and migrations. They retain existing configuration and data. The installer remembers successful market initialization for the same registry identity and migration version. A run with --skip-market-init leaves that stage available for a later run.

items.title: Use an existing PostgreSQL server
items.text:
PostgreSQL 14 or newer is required. With a matching credential already configured, the installer uses that connection without installing a local server or changing its service. A valid registry is checked for name, purpose, identity, and migration history before migrations. An explicitly selected empty database with schema creation privileges can be initialized. An existing database with user objects and no Forge history needs an administrator’s review. The installer refuses to adopt it.

For local provisioning without credentials, the installer uses one running APT cluster or a Homebrew PostgreSQL server on the default socket and port. It can install and start a new server through the native backend. It creates an unprivileged, dedicated owner role and the database marketforge or marketforge_test. If the target name already exists, configure its verified credential or use a different approved production database. The installer leaves existing clusters, roles, and authentication settings in place.

./install.sh --skip-postgres
./install.sh --dev --skip-postgres --skip-market-init

items.title: PostgreSQL credentials
items.text:
Database infrastructure resolves credentials automatically, in this order:

  1. A nonempty environment variable.
  2. The same key in <project-root>/.secrets/postgres.env.
  3. An explicit configuration error if neither supplies a value.

Blank environment values allow file fallback. Production is the default and uses PRODUCTION_DATABASE_KEY. Pass --testing to use TEST_DATABASE_KEY. Use --production to select production explicitly. The flags are mutually exclusive and each environment uses its own key.

The file is read as dotenv data, never executed or sourced. Ordinary assignments, optional export, whitespace, comments and single/double quoted values are supported. Shell commands and variable references remain literal; no interpolation occurs. The file is resolved through project-root discovery or the CLI's --project-root, so database commands also work from repository subdirectories or another directory with an explicit root. Local provisioning adds the generated credential to the file with mode 0600, preserving unrelated entries. Use a dedicated role and keep this file private and out of version control.

items.title: Inspect a database
items.text:
Run mf database status for production or mf database status --testing for testing. Credentials must explicitly name the database. Forge compares that name with the server response, verifies the stored database UUID and purpose in forge_meta.database_identity, and checks applied migration checksums. Testing additionally requires the database name marketforge_test.

If PostgreSQL is unreachable, check role access, network access, and which key is set in the process environment. If the name or purpose check fails, verify the credential assignment with the database administrator. For a newly provisioned database, review schema availability before applying migrations with mf database migrate --production or mf database migrate --testing. Status checks and TUI startup are read-only with respect to the registry. Production initialization requires a verified registry with all migrations already applied.

items.title: Manual installation
items.text:
Use this route to manage packages, tools, and PostgreSQL yourself. Install Neovim, Python 3.12 or newer, uv, Rust 1.89 or newer, and the native compiler tools. Provision a PostgreSQL connection as described above.

uv sync --project forge --locked --no-default-groups
uv run --project forge --locked --no-default-groups mf engine build normalize
uv run --project forge --locked --no-default-groups mf engine build merge
uv run --project forge --locked --no-default-groups mf engine build convert

Use the environment's executable directly or prefix the commands below with uv run --project forge --locked --no-default-groups. For a production registry, review its status before applying migrations or initializing market data.

mf database status
mf database migrate --production
mf init --production

items.title: Prepare the testing registry
items.text:
Create a dedicated database named marketforge_test and give its intended role the privileges to own its objects and apply migrations. Configure TEST_DATABASE_KEY, then run:

mf database migrate --testing
mf database status --testing
mf doctor --testing

Confirm purpose testing and zero pending migrations. Use mf init --testing when you are ready to collect metadata.

items.title: Inspection and notebook tools
items.text:
The development installer includes these tools. For a standard or manual installation, install Arrow in the Forge environment for datasets schema and datasets head:

uv pip install --python .install/runtime/bin/python 'pyarrow>=18'

For a manual Forge environment, point --python at that environment’s interpreter. Use --dev if you also want Polars and JupyterLab.

items.title: Verify and troubleshoot
items.text:
Run mf normalize profiles list to inspect the installed normalization catalogue locally. Before compiling a custom profile, check the managed normalizer with mf engine status. The profile authoring guide covers the draft and validation steps.

mf --help
nvim --version | head -n 1
mf config show
mf engine status
mf database status

Check that all three Engine targets are verified. For a development install, use mf database status --testing and open mf tui --testing.

  • If mf is unavailable, use the absolute launcher path and check which installation your PATH selects.
  • If a selected local cluster is stopped or ambiguous, inspect it with the local administrator. Supply the intended connection and use --skip-postgres.
  • If a configured registry is rejected, check the credential key, database name, purpose, and migration history before retrying. See database troubleshooting.
  • If a newer toolchain is required, update the active toolchain deliberately, then rerun. A verified binary with an unsupported runtime option needs a managed rebuild using the current checkout.

Continue with the Bybit quick start.

items.title: First dataset: Bybit BTCUSDT trades and depth
items.text: Acquire one UTC day of trades and L2 depth for Bybit’s BTCUSDT linear USDT perpetual. Normalize it into canonical Parquet, verify the registered primary files, then check the first reconstructed book state against its retained boundary.
path: First dataset: Bybit trades and depth

items.title: Prepare the workspace
items.text:
From the checkout, run ./install.sh --dev --skip-market-init to set up the managed Engine, Arrow, and a migrated testing registry. If you already have a standard installation and want to add only the prerequisites for this guide, follow manual testing setup and inspection tools. Keep that registry selected with --testing throughout this example. Use a workspace with space for both compressed archives, normalized Parquet, and Engine scratch files.

The installed profiles must match this venue and contract. Validate them before downloading:

mf normalize profiles validate bybit.perpetual.linear.trades
mf normalize profiles validate bybit.perpetual.linear.depth

The catalogue identifies this instrument as bybit.perpetual.linear.BTCUSDT. The acquisition recipe uses the native symbol with separate venue, instrument type and market category fields. It requests trades and order_book_l2; the Engine depth profile ends in .depth.
path: First dataset: Bybit trades and depth

items.title: Plan and acquire a day
items.text:
Use the Bybit recipe for the half-open UTC interval [2026-10-27T00:00:00Z, 2026-10-28T00:00:00Z). Discovery selects whole overlapping daily archives. A shorter interval inside this day can still select both complete archives. Normalization processes the selected inputs without trimming their records to the request.

recipe=docs/content/examples/bybit/acquisition.toml
library=data/.config/workflows/data_engineering/acquisition
name=bybit-btc-20261027
mkdir -p "$library"
if [ ! -e "$library/$name.toml" ]; then
  cp "$recipe" "$library/$name.toml"
fi
cmp "$recipe" "$library/$name.toml"

If cmp reports a difference, choose an unused name and repeat the copy before proceeding.

mf acquisition map "$name" --testing
mf acquisition plan "$name" --testing --cache-only

Map contacts Bybit for discovery and records the result without downloading archive bodies. The plan reads registered discovery and local inventory. Check that the two requests resolve to the expected candidates before downloading:

Request Expected archive Trades BTCUSDT2026-10-27.csv.gz L2 depth 2026-10-27_BTCUSDT_ob200.data.zip 
mf acquisition download "$name" --testing
mf storage list --testing --exchange bybit --instrument-type perpetual \
  --market linear --instrument BTCUSDT --status complete --wide \
  --start 2026-10-27T00:00:00Z --end 2026-10-28T00:00:00Z

Download registers verified managed copies. Check for both filenames in storage. Use a returned local ID with mf storage show LOCAL_ID --testing to inspect the managed path and checksum. The historical acquisition guide explains discovery and retries. The storage guide explains local records and verification.
path: First dataset: Bybit trades and depth

items.title: Resolve specification evidence
items.text:
Preparation needs a catalogue entry and instrument specification evidence applicable to the selected archives. A fresh, dedicated testing workspace can use Forge initialization after acquisition so enrichment can consider the newly registered files:

mf --json init --testing > bybit-init.json
mf markets show bybit.linear.BTCUSDT --testing
mf catalog specs show bybit.perpetual.linear.BTCUSDT --testing

Initialization collects market metadata from providers, attempts historical metadata enrichment, and publishes standard rankings. Review the recorded stages even if ranking fails after catalogue collection. Use catalogue declarations if you have verified historical terms to register. An inferred applicability decision is a reproducible policy decision. It does not establish that the exchange’s terms were historically verified. Read identity and historical applicability for that distinction.
path: First dataset: Bybit trades and depth

items.title: Prepare and run normalization
items.text:
mf normalize prepare "$recipe" --testing --dry-run | cpout

Look for a prepared plan with separate trades and depth jobs. Resolve any reported blockers before execution. The dry run previews the plan and prospective paths. The execution command prepares and validates its own batch.

mf --json normalize execute "$recipe" --testing > bybit-result.json

Forge retains the submitted batch and execution evidence. A complete result with verification = "verified" and registration = "registered" records the verified normalized publications and their registered file IDs. Use those IDs in the same database environment.
path: First dataset: Bybit trades and depth

items.title: Verify both outputs
items.text:
python - <<'PY' > bybit-file-ids.txt
import json
from pathlib import Path

result = json.loads(Path("bybit-result.json").read_text())
assert result["status"] == "complete", result["status"]
assert result["verification"] == "verified", result["verification"]
assert result["registration"] == "registered", result["registration"]
assert result["registrations"], "No primary files were registered"
for item in result["registrations"]:
    print(item["catalogue_dataset_id"])
PY
while IFS= read -r id; do
  mf datasets show "$id" --testing
  mf datasets schema "$id" --testing
  mf datasets head "$id" --testing --limit 3 --precise
  mf datasets streams "$id" --testing
  mf datasets verify "$id" --testing
done < bybit-file-ids.txt

Look for both content types and inspect the manifests referenced by the result. Several primary files can share one publication manifest. Trades carry a trade ID and exact decimal values. Depth rows describe level changes, while the event index maps book observations to row spans. One observation can emit many levels or zero rows, so source record counts, indexed observation counts, and emitted row counts can differ.

Run the depth inspection script on this example’s report:

python docs/content/examples/bybit/inspect_depth.py bybit-result.json

On a retained run for this recipe, the script matched 400 initial levels to the saved boundary. Your actual row counts and file IDs come from your own run report. It establishes the initial book state for this publication. Continuous reconstruction and external historical coverage require additional depth evidence. Compare the requested interval, reported nominal source coverage, and observed output bounds separately.
path: First dataset: Bybit trades and depth

items.title: Recover and continue
items.text:
• If discovery fails, inspect the map report and provider availability before retrying. A cache miss alone cannot establish archive unavailability.
  • If preparation is blocked, follow the selected archive’s diagnostics for missing inputs, profiles, or applicable specifications.
  • If the Engine committed output but registration failed, retain the execution intent and retry registration only against the original registry.

Continue with normalize historical data to adapt this workflow or inspect datasets to work with the output.
path: First dataset: Bybit trades and depth

items.title: MarketForge reference
items.text:
Look up the interface at the boundary you are working with. Use the guides for end-to-end procedures.

Interface Canonical lookup Forge CLI Command index and shared conventions Editable configuration Application settings and operation recipes Profiles and managed registration Profile schema · Registration declarations Runtime interpretation Resources, integrity and reconciliation Generated inputs and retained run state Prepared contracts Committed data Publication formats Python readers Python dataset API
