Use mf normalize profiles list to find an installed interpretation for the raw layout. To author a missing interpretation, run mf normalize profiles guide trades or mf normalize profiles guide depth. Follow the profile workflow and use the schema reference when choosing field types and transformations. After registration, prepare normalization.

For types, defaults and native identity fields, see the registration recipe reference.

items.title: Inspect and apply a registration plan
Native Identity Sampling
items.text: When native identity is supplied, registration preflight can check the corresponding fields against bounded source samples.

items.title: Why is this useful?
items.text:
Suppose a recipe declares:

publisher_id = 2
instrument_id = 38

but the sampled source records contain a different publisher or instrument ID.

This may indicate that the wrong file was selected or the declaration is incorrect.

Registration can detect such mismatches during preflight.

items.title: Does sampling read the entire file?
items.text:
No.

The supported source-layout check is bounded.

It does not independently verify every record in an arbitrarily large recording.

items.title: Does every source format support native identity sampling?
items.text:
Not necessarily.

The current bounded sampler supports particular CSV and JSONL identity paths.

For example, the specialized XLSX sample path does not provide the same native identity sampling behavior.

items.title: What happens if the source format is unsupported?
items.text:
Registration reports the applicable source or sampling incompatibility.

Do not bypass the check by inventing field names.

items.title: Does successful sampling guarantee complete source validity?
items.text:
No.

A bounded sample can establish useful evidence about selected records.

Complete record processing and integrity evaluation belong to normalization.

items.title: Register AAPL Trades and MBP-10 Recordings
items.text:
The repository contains a more realistic registration example using Databento XNAS.ITCH data.

The source files are:

.recordings/
├── AAPL_trades.jsonl
└── AAPL_orderbook_L2.jsonl

They represent the historical interval:

2024-10-28 14:30:00 UTC
through
2024-10-28 14:40:00 UTC

The end is exclusive.

items.title: Source provenance
items.text:
The recording was supplied by Databento.

The execution venue is Nasdaq.

The instrument is AAPL.

The source-native identifiers include:

publisher_id = 2
instrument_id = 38

These values are scoped to the relevant source recording.

items.title: Why is this example important?
items.text:
It demonstrates the distinction between:

  • Market-data provider.
  • Execution venue.
  • Canonical instrument identity.
  • Source-native instrument identity.
  • Source-format profile.

All of these are represented separately.

items.title: Complete Databento Registration Recipe
items.text:
Save this as:

data/.config/workflows/data_engineering/import/registration/databento-aapl.toml

[registration]
version = 1
name = "databento-aapl"

[source]
key = "databento-xnas-itch-aapl-20241028"
provider = "Databento"
product = "XNAS.ITCH"
kind = "recording"
root = ".recordings"
provenance = "User-supplied Databento Trades and MBP-10 JSONL exports for 2024-10-28. Publisher ID 2 and native instrument ID 38 are scoped to these source files."

[coverage]
start = 2024-10-28T14:30:00Z
end = 2024-10-28T14:40:00Z

[[inputs]]
instrument = "xnas.equity.equity.AAPL"
profile = "xnas.equity.equity.trades"
content = "trades"
files = ["AAPL_trades.jsonl"]

[inputs.native_identity]
namespace = "databento:XNAS.ITCH:2024-10-28"
publisher_field = "hd.publisher_id"
publisher_id = 2
instrument_field = "hd.instrument_id"
instrument_id = 38
provenance = "Header identity in the supplied XNAS.ITCH exports."

[[inputs]]
instrument = "xnas.equity.equity.AAPL"
profile = "xnas.equity.equity.depth"
content = "depth"
files = ["AAPL_orderbook_L2.jsonl"]

[inputs.native_identity]
namespace = "databento:XNAS.ITCH:2024-10-28"
publisher_field = "hd.publisher_id"
publisher_id = 2
instrument_field = "hd.instrument_id"
instrument_id = 38
provenance = "Header identity in the supplied XNAS.ITCH exports."

This is the complete registration recipe supplied with the repository's Databento example.

items.title: What is registered?
items.text: Input Instrument Profile Native identity Trades AAPL xnas.equity.equity.trades Publisher 2, instrument 38 Depth AAPL xnas.equity.equity.depth Publisher 2, instrument 38

items.title: Why do both inputs use the same native IDs?
items.text:
Both recordings describe the same source-native instrument under the declared publisher and product namespace.

However, they contain different market-data content.

items.title: Why use separate profiles?
items.text:
The trade and depth records have different structures and normalization requirements.

The trade profile interprets executions.

The depth profile interprets the corresponding order-book observations.

items.title: Does Databento become the exchange?
items.text:
No.

The instrument reference remains:

xnas.equity.equity.AAPL

The provider is recorded separately:

provider = "Databento"

items.title: Does registration require the original Databento API?
items.text:
No.

This workflow operates on the supplied local files.

It does not need to download the same files again.

items.title: Important prerequisites
items.text:
Before executing this recipe, make sure:

  • The source files exist.
  • XNAS is registered.
  • AAPL is registered.
  • Applicable historical specifications are available.
  • The trade profile is installed.
  • The depth profile is installed.
  • The profile quantity encodings agree with the specifications.

See the Databento example for the complete setup.

items.title: Structural Validation vs. Registration Preflight
items.text:
A registration recipe must satisfy several levels of validation.

These checks are different.

items.title: Structural validation
items.text:
Checks the TOML declaration itself.

For example:

  • Required fields.
  • Supported version.
  • Input array structure.
  • Instrument reference format.
  • Profile ID matching.
  • File-selection presence.
  • Specification fingerprint syntax.
  • Native identity field types.

items.title: Source inspection
items.text:
Checks the declared local files.

For example:

  • Source root.
  • Selected paths.
  • File count.
  • Physical file identity.
  • Duplicate inputs.

items.title: Registration preflight
items.text:
Uses the testing registry and installed profiles to check the complete registration binding.

For example:

  • Registered instrument identity.
  • Explicit historical specification evidence.
  • Profile installation.
  • Rust semantic profile validation.
  • Quantity encoding compatibility.
  • Bounded source-layout compatibility.
  • Existing source registration conflicts.

items.title: Why separate these checks?
items.text:
Different errors require different information.

For example, a missing TOML field can be detected locally.

A missing historical specification requires a database lookup.

A profile compilation error requires the Rust normalizer.

A source-layout mismatch requires inspecting the selected file.

Keeping these stages distinct makes failures easier to diagnose.

items.title: Register and normalize manually supplied data
items.text: Raw registration copies and verifies bytes; it does not normalize them. Profiles describe interpretation, registration recipes declare source/provenance and reference existing catalogue metadata, normalization recipes select registered inputs, and prepared JSON is the exact Rust workload contract. Normalization runtime policy lives in data/.config/engine/normalize.toml.
path: Register and normalize manually supplied data

items.title: Synthetic shared-instrument example
items.text: Use the synthetic trade and depth bundle for complete source files, catalogue declarations and executable commands. Its fictional venue has an independent profile namespace.
path: Register and normalize manually supplied data

items.title: Ownership, history and recovery
items.text:
Provider/recorder and product/feed are distinct from trading venue. Registration never substitutes external for a venue, fabricates a URL/discovery membership, refreshes current market metadata or supplies missing historical specifications. Coverage declarations are separate from observed timestamp bounds and continuity. An interval crossing a specification change cannot silently select one version. Unsupported classes/venues/layouts remain blockers.

Migration 0013_unified_forge.sql evolves the existing registry without moving raw bytes. raw_objects is the source-object authority; remote IDs retain their values. Legacy local IDs map explicitly through legacy_raw_identity_map. raw_sources, immutable raw_interpretations, local_archives and append-only raw_bindings retain provenance, physical revisions and interpretation revisions. remote_archives and external_archives are compatibility views; acquisition and registration writes target the shared tables. Existing storage browsing, verification, cleanup and database backups retain local-copy identities and paths. Legacy import commands use the same copy/source-object services, but old format drafts remain unapproved and must be replaced with manually authored schema-2 profiles and full registration declarations for normalization.

Do not migrate a shared testing database underneath another process. Use the existing migration workflow during a coordinated maintenance window. Integration tests instead apply the full chain in operation-owned disposable schemas on the positively verified testing database. Production is not migrated by these commands.

Planning freezes submitted declarations and bounded inventory in an operation-owned directory, with no copies/profile installation/registration rows. Run independently freezes and revalidates its own inventory; it does not silently apply a previously edited plan artifact. Copying uses bounded buffers and before/after source stability evidence. Registration never adopts originals in place or moves/deletes them. Recoverable copy reservations retain intended destinations/checksums before publication. Retries reuse unchanged verified bytes; changed bytes produce revisions. New bindings can reuse the same physical copy, retaining old downstream interpretation evidence.

The register workflow checks catalogue identity, historical applicability, and the installed profile before publishing any managed copies. Use the legacy raw-only import when interpretation is incomplete. A run retains submitted recipe, intent, copy receipts and outcome under data/runs/register-*; retry the same recipe to recover. Environment provenance remains testing, with no production fallback.

For all command syntax, execution receipts, automatic dataset registration, Degraded integrity, partial sessions and registration-only recovery, see the Forge command reference.
path: Register and normalize manually supplied data

items.title: Acquire historical archives
items.text:
Acquisition finds historical market-data archives and preserves the original provider bytes in managed raw storage. Once the files are available locally, normalization reads them and builds canonical datasets.

Create → Edit → Validate → Discover → Download → Inspect → Normalize

Run the commands from your MarketForge workspace. The examples use the testing registry, where downloads still write real files to the configured data root. See the acquisition prerequisites for setup.

items.title: 1. Create a recipe
items.text:
mf acquisition new september | cpout
mf acquisition edit september

new creates a TOML recipe in the workspace acquisition library and refuses to overwrite an existing file. edit opens that file in your editor and checks its structure when the editor exits successfully.

A recipe has one time interval shared by all its requests. Each request names an exchange, instrument type, market category, data type, and archive scope. This example selects one UTC day of Bybit BTCUSDT linear perpetual trades. The interval includes its start and excludes its end. Use the example as a starting point and replace the dates and request details with the data you intend to acquire.

version = 1

[interval]
start = 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z
end = 2026-09-02T00:00:00Z

[[requests]]
exchange = "bybit"
instrument_type = "perpetual"
market_category = "linear"
data_type = "trades"
scope = { kind = "instrument", identifier = "BTCUSDT" }

Choose combinations with mf acquisition sources or the supported historical sources. See the configuration reference for every recipe field.

items.title: 2. Validate
items.text:
mf acquisition validate september | cpout

Validation reads the saved TOML and checks fields, types, and interval order. A structurally valid recipe can still specify an unsupported source combination or a date with no published files. Mapping evaluates the combination and checks for archives.

items.title: 3. Discover archives
items.text:
mf acquisition map september --testing

Mapping finds archive identities and records their nominal time intervals without downloading archive bodies. The request table distinguishes cached discovery from discovery performed during this run. A successful search can be empty. Unsupported requests and discovery failures have separate outcomes. Use the run ID or report path in the summary to inspect every request.

items.title: 4. Download
items.text:
mf acquisition download september --testing

Download uses fresh discovery when available and discovers archives as needed. It verifies the size and SHA-256 of matching local copies before reusing them. New upstream revisions get separate immutable managed copies. Acquisition retrieves whole archives that overlap your interval, so a file may contain records beyond the requested dates.

items.title: 5. Inspect
items.text:
mf storage list --testing --exchange bybit --instrument BTCUSDT --data-type trades | cpout
mf runs list --testing --operation acquisition --limit 10 | cpout
mf runs report RUN_ID --testing | cpout

Storage shows registered files. Use the run ID from the acquisition summary to inspect discovery and file outcomes. Nominal archive intervals describe the advertised file boundaries. Event-level completeness remains unknown even when those intervals span the entire request.

items.title: Optional operations
items.text: Goal Command or option Inspect fresh cached discovery mf acquisition plan september --testing --cache-only Hash a bounded sample of registered files locally Add --verify-local to the cache-only plan. Check discovery again Add --refresh to map or download. Lower HTTP request pacing Add --requests-per-second 0.5 to map or download. Capture machine-readable results Put global --json before acquisition. Add --silent to map or download to suppress progress in human mode.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom What to do No archives found Check the native identifier, scope and dates. Use --refresh if cached results need an upstream check. Unsupported source or scope Check the historical source matrix and update the request. Partial or failed download Inspect the retained report and events, then follow the recovery instructions. Invalid recipe Correct the TOML location or field reported by validate. See common validation errors.

items.title: Next step
items.text: Normalize managed archives into canonical datasets.

items.title: Managing acquisitions
items.text: Use the acquisition guide for the first run. This page covers discovery freshness, managed copies, and recovery.

items.title: Discovery cache and refresh
items.text:
A completed scan is fresh for six hours when its source scope, covering interval, and adapter version match. A successful empty scan is cacheable. Unsupported requests and partial or failed scans do not provide reusable completed coverage.

mf acquisition map september --testing --refresh
mf acquisition plan september --testing --cache-only --verify-local --limit 20 | cpout

A successful refresh supersedes overlapping completed discovery for that selection. A failed refresh leaves previous completed discovery intact. Refresh updates discovery evidence. Download can still reuse matching verified bytes.

The optional cache-only plan reads fresh completed scans from the selected registry. Unresolved requests need discovery. The archive list is a bounded sample (default 100, range 1–10000). With --verify-local, planning checks size and SHA-256 on eligible local copies in that sample without updating the registry. Use mapping to discover current upstream availability.

items.title: Archive identity and managed copies
items.text:
An archive's source identity includes its provider-native object key and revision evidence. Download URLs can expire or change independently of that identity. A changed upstream revision gets a separate managed copy. Changes that the provider exposes without distinct revision evidence may go undetected.

Download verifies matching completed local files by size and SHA-256 before reuse. If a matching copy is missing or corrupt, the registry records that condition. A needed download can renew an expired or missing source location. Forge checks supported container integrity and publishes verified bytes as immutable managed raw files, then finalizes their local archive registration.

Storage lists registered copies and their states. Nominal intervals describe the published archive boundaries. Even gap-free nominal intervals leave record integrity and market-event completeness unknown.

mf storage list --testing --exchange bybit --instrument BTCUSDT --wide | cpout
mf storage show LOCAL_ID --testing | cpout
mf storage coverage --testing --exchange bybit --instrument BTCUSDT --data-type trades --gaps | cpout

Use the local archive ID returned by the list command. See storage commands for inspection, verification and cleanup options.

items.title: Inspect runs and reports
items.text:
mf runs list --testing --operation acquisition --limit 10 | cpout
mf runs show RUN_ID --testing | cpout
mf runs report RUN_ID --testing | cpout
mf runs logs RUN_ID --testing --limit 50 | cpout

Use the run ID from the acquisition result. The execution index provides searchable status. The report and recorded events contain detailed request and file outcomes. The download byte total covers measured completed transfers. Failed or interrupted transfers can consume additional bandwidth. The report path points into the configured data root's runs/ directory. The event log is a bounded read of retained events. See execution history and retained evidence.

items.title: Recover partial or failed runs
items.text:
1. Read the report and events. Identify unsupported requests, successful empty searches, discovery failures and file failures separately. A partial run can leave completed copies available for reuse. A hard termination can leave a reservation without a final report.
  2. Correct unsupported scopes in the recipe. For rate or network errors, let the provider cooldown expire before retrying. Forge uses bounded retries and honors cooldowns. Add --requests-per-second 0.5 to lower pacing when appropriate. Provider budgets still apply.
  3. Verify a suspect local copy, or reconcile an interrupted publication when a local archive ID is available.
  4. Rerun mf acquisition download september --testing to reuse verified files and retrieve outstanding archives. An incomplete HTTP transfer starts again from the beginning.
mf storage verify --testing --archive LOCAL_ID | cpout
mf storage reconcile --testing --archive LOCAL_ID | cpout

Verification reads local bytes and can update registry state. Reconciliation uses durable size and hash evidence to recover an eligible reservation, publish a verified temporary file, or finalize registration. Both are local maintenance operations. Partials without sufficient evidence remain unverified.

items.title: Cleanup
items.text: Use the storage cleanup reference to preview failed attempts with storage prune or managed copies with storage delete. Apply cleanup only after reviewing the selected targets and any dependencies. See the Forge workflow for dataset build and registration recovery.

items.title: Manual catalogue registration
items.text:
Register the execution venue, its instrument, applicable historical specifications, and each required Rust profile before registering external archives. The order matters because PostgreSQL assigns the exchange and instrument IDs and creates a canonical historical instrument mapping when it inserts the instrument. A profile identifies a venue and market category and can be installed once that venue exists.

Use the testing database and install the managed Rust validator first.

mf database migrate --testing
mf engine build normalize

Catalogue registration requires no API adapter, market statistics, or ranking snapshot. Initialization collects only the venues and scopes that have API adapters. A provider such as Databento distributes data, while the venue is the explicit execution identity. Publisher and provider details belong in source provenance. Source-native instrument IDs are scoped to their publisher and source and are independent of PostgreSQL IDs.

The linked files use an AAPL-shaped equity identity at a fictional venue and two synthetic source records. Their economics are demonstration values. Use verified declarations and source evidence for real recordings.

  • Exchange and instrument
  • Current and historical specifications
  • Trades and L2 depth profiles
  • Register external archives

items.title: Exchanges and instruments
items.text:
Declare the execution venue in exchange.toml. The exchange code is the stable key and uses lowercase letters, digits, and underscores. Exact re-registration returns the same ID. A different name under the same code is rejected.

code = "example_exchange"
name = "Example Exchange"

mf catalog exchange validate --file docs/content/examples/catalogue/exchange.toml
mf catalog exchange add --from docs/content/examples/catalogue/exchange.toml --testing
mf catalog exchange list --testing
mf catalog exchange show example_exchange --testing

The instrument declaration uses an exchange code, a market category, an instrument type, and the native symbol. For an equity, both category fields are equity. The optional settlement asset belongs to the execution instrument if applicable. PostgreSQL returns the catalogue ID and the historical authority ID. Conflicting properties under the same instrument identity are rejected.

exchange = "example_exchange"
symbol = "AAPL"
instrument_type = "equity"
market_category = "equity"
base_asset = "AAPL"
quote_asset = "USD"
status = "active"

mf catalog instrument validate --file docs/content/examples/catalogue/instrument.toml
mf catalog instrument add --from docs/content/examples/catalogue/instrument.toml --testing
mf catalog instrument list --testing
mf --json catalog instrument show example_exchange.equity.equity.AAPL --testing

items.title: Depth profile sample checks
items.text:
Start with the complete depth profile and run the recording check. Compare the starting levels with the snapshot. Apply the emitted update rows in order and check that replacement, deletion, and insertion produce the expected final levels.

When working with a bounded observation, compare both sides as recorded at one instant and check the observation span in the publication evidence. For a sequenced feed, add a fixture that exercises a real ordering boundary such as a documented reset or the beginning of a new range. Bounded observations · Sequence policies

items.title: Trade profile sample checks
items.text:
Start with the complete trade profile and run the recording check. Compare the first record in the registered dataset with the source row. The dataset preview can expose a reversed side mapping or a quantity that was interpreted in the wrong units even when compilation passed.

For a signed feed, include one buy and one sell in the sample. Verify the decoded side and quantity independently. If the source provides a native trade ID, include two different trades with the same timestamp in the check so you can confirm that identity comes from the native field. Side transforms · Native trade ID scope

items.title: Troubleshoot normalization profiles
items.text:
Use the authoring guide for draft creation, Rust validation, installation, and the sample check. Start here when the compiler rejects a definition or a known raw value differs from the emitted record.

mf engine status | cpout
mf normalize profiles list --exchange binance --type trades | cpout
mf normalize profiles validate binance.spot.spot.trades | cpout

To inspect an installed file in read-only Neovim, run mf normalize profiles inspect binance.spot.spot.trades. To inspect only its text, use mf normalize profiles show binance.spot.spot.trades | cpout. Use the CLI reference for the full syntax.

items.title: Profile ID has too many components
items.text:
Cause: The ID contains an unsupported variant or version component.

For example:

binance.spot.spot.trades.custom

is invalid.

Use exactly:

exchange.instrument_type.market_category.trades|depth

items.title: Filename does not match ID
items.text:
Cause: The filename differs from the internal profile identity.

Use the exact required filename:

<profile-id>.toml

items.title: Instrument type and market category disagree
items.text:
Cause: The declared combination is invalid.

For example, an equity profile must use the equity market category.

items.title: Format code is rejected
items.text:
Cause: The code does not match the supported exchange prefix, content letter, or positive-number rule.

Use the format code associated with the actual source.

items.title: Installation conflicts with an existing profile
items.text:
Cause: The same profile ID already has a different compiled interpretation.

Inspect the installed definition and resolve the conflict explicitly.

Do not invent another ID component or overwrite the installed file manually.

items.title: Unsupported record format
items.text:
Cause: The selected format and record layout do not form a supported decoder combination.

For example, arbitrary headered CSV depth input is not automatically available.

Use an existing compatible profile as the starting point.

items.title: Incorrect source container
items.text:
Cause: The profile declares the wrong packaging type.

For example, a ZIP archive is declared as plain CSV.

Inspect the actual source container.

items.title: Header mismatch
items.text:
Cause: The profile expects headers that do not match the source file.

For headered trade CSV, use the actual header field names.

items.title: Invalid positional fields
items.text:
Cause: Headerless CSV positions are duplicated, missing, or noncontiguous.

Use 1-based positions covering every declared physical column.

items.title: Unsupported sorting
items.text:
Cause: The profile declares timestamp-sortable ordering for a source whose runtime path cannot safely sort its stateful events.

Use the actual supported source-ordering contract.

items.title: Timestamps are incorrect
items.text:
Possible cause: The profile uses the wrong timestamp encoding.

Check whether the source uses:

seconds
milliseconds
microseconds
nanoseconds
ISO 8601

Do not infer the unit solely from the exchange name.

items.title: ISO timestamps fail
items.text:
Possible cause: The source lacks a timezone or the declarations do not satisfy the supported ISO timestamp requirements.

Use the correct source encoding.

items.title: Trade quantities are too large or too small
items.text:
Possible cause: The source denomination is wrong.

For example, a contract count may have been treated as base-asset quantity.

Inspect the actual quantity encoding and applicable instrument specifications.

items.title: Spot profile declares contracts
items.text:
Cause: Spot profiles cannot use contract quantity encoding.

Use the correct supported quantity interpretation.

items.title: Contract value is missing
items.text:
Cause: The source uses contract quantities but the processing job lacks authoritative contract-value information.

Resolve the relevant instrument specifications through the catalogue.

Do not hardcode an invented multiplier into the profile.

items.title: Side mapping is reversed
items.text:
Cause: The source-side convention was misunderstood.

Consult the provider's actual trade-side semantics.

items.title: Unmapped side value
items.text:
Cause: The source contains a value not covered by the explicit mapping.

Add the correct supported mapping only after establishing its meaning.

items.title: casefold does not accept a value
items.text:
Cause: The source value falls outside the supported buy/sell vocabulary.

Do not assume arbitrary whitespace trimming or custom case normalization.

items.title: Signed quantity has zero side
items.text:
Cause: Zero does not establish positive or negative direction.

Investigate the source semantics rather than assigning an arbitrary side.

items.title: Trade ID scope is invalid
items.text:
Cause: The declaration uses an unsupported reset-domain combination or lacks the required trade ID mapping.

Check the selected native identity contract.

items.title: Source-local IDs were treated as global
items.text:
Cause: The profile claims stronger uniqueness than the source guarantees.

Use a scope supported by actual source evidence.

items.title: A record matches no rule
items.text:
Cause: The event filters do not cover the source's actual event type.

Inspect the source values and supported rule mappings.

items.title: A record matches multiple rules
items.text:
Cause: Filters overlap.

Make the rule selections disjoint.

Rule order does not resolve ambiguous matches.

items.title: Snapshot and update are confused
items.text:
Cause: The event classifier maps the source to the wrong target.

Verify the source's snapshot and incremental-update semantics.

items.title: Book levels are incorrect
items.text:
Cause: The profile uses the wrong array element order or object field names.

Inspect level_format and level_fields.

items.title: Absolute quantities accumulate incorrectly
items.text:
Cause: Absolute updates were treated as relative changes.

For an absolute-level source, the supplied quantity replaces the level quantity.

items.title: Relative updates fail
items.text:
Cause: The source layout is not supported by the current relative-update decoder.

The implemented path is specialized for supported scalar CSV sources.

items.title: Sequence errors appear unexpectedly
items.text:
Cause: The profile declares the wrong sequence policy.

For example, a source may allow jumps while the profile declares consecutive sequencing.

Use the source's documented sequence contract.

items.title: Missing snapshot
items.text:
Cause: Incremental updates cannot be initialized according to the required reconstruction rules.

Check the source archive and snapshot availability.

Do not invent an initial book state.

items.title: Bounded observation is treated as full depth
items.text:
Cause: The source's top-N limitation was ignored.

Preserve the actual bounded depth semantics.

items.title: XLSX profile fails
items.text:
Possible cause: The workbook does not match the fixed supported layout.

Check:

  • One worksheet.
  • Headers.
  • Required field names.
  • Unix-second timestamps.
  • Supported ascending ordering.

items.title: Mixed-instrument XLSX fails
items.text:
Cause: The current runtime does not support XLSX family routing.

Use a supported source-specific workflow.

items.title: Gate.io feed variant fails
items.text:
Cause: The selected variant is incomplete or does not match the requested source feed.

Each variant must provide its own complete source, field, and normalization declarations.

items.title: Native instrument lookup fails
items.text:
Cause: The corresponding concrete instrument is unavailable in the prepared job's catalogue.

lookup = "catalog" does not fetch missing exchange metadata.

Resolve the historical instrument identity and specifications first.

items.title: Normalization profiles
items.text:
Follow Create a normalization profile for source inspection, complete trade and depth examples, validation, and installation. Use the field index to adapt the examples to another source layout.

Task Start here Check actual trade values Trade sample checks Check book initialization and updates Depth sample checks Diagnose a compiler or runtime error Profile troubleshooting Find a CLI option Profile commands

items.title: Instrument specifications
items.text:
Use a quoted decimal or an exact TOML integer for economic values. An instrument declaration supplies the default base, quote, and settlement assets. Derivative quantities expressed in contracts require an explicit value and denomination. Historical declarations need provenance and an inclusive start and exclusive end. An observation timestamp can be supplied when known.

Example historical specification for synthetic AAPL data:

instrument = "example_exchange.equity.equity.AAPL"
quantity_type = "base"
tick_size = "0.01"
qty_step = "1"
valid_from = 2024-10-28T00:00:00Z
valid_to = 2024-10-29T00:00:00Z
provenance = "Synthetic example parameters for the example files only"

mf catalog specs validate --file docs/content/examples/catalogue/specs.toml
mf catalog specs add --from docs/content/examples/catalogue/specs.toml --testing
mf catalog specs list --testing
mf --json catalog specs show example_exchange.equity.equity.AAPL --testing

Historical declarations are immutable and retain their evidence IDs and fingerprints. Conflicting overlapping revisions are rejected. An adjacent or disjoint interval can carry a different specification. Exact repeat submissions reuse the existing evidence. Archive registration requires a single applicable declaration that covers the whole interval.

To register a current observation, omit both validity fields and supply the actual fetched_at or as_of time. A newer observation advances the current catalogue row. An older one is retained as evidence. Current evidence carries no historical validity and does not qualify an external archive for registration.

items.title: Markets and statistics
items.text:
Markets provides an instrument catalogue and retained current observations. It is separate from historical archive acquisition: a ticker refresh does not download trade/order-book archives, and a current listing is not proof of historical availability.

Information Purpose Instrument metadata Native identity, assets, market/type, contract specification, lifecycle and status. Current statistics Last price, available rolling volumes/turnover, and optional open interest/funding, with units and timing evidence. Historical archives Source files covering nominal historical intervals, managed by acquisition. Ranking snapshots Immutable selections and ordering computed from retained observations under a named policy.

Begin with instrument discovery, then statistics interpretation and rankings. Use the markets configuration and CLI reference for exact settings and options.

items.title: Prerequisites and effects
items.text:
Install Forge and configure the guarded testing database. The markets sync, refresh, list, and show commands default to production. Pass --testing for the testing registry. Ranking file creation and validation work without a database.

  • sync retrieves public instrument metadata and writes catalogue/sync records.
  • refresh retrieves current statistics and appends observations; run a matching successful sync first.
  • list and show browse stored data without network access or registry mutation.
  • rank build writes a published snapshot using stored observations; it does not refresh.
  • rank update retrieves statistics and publishes standard policy snapshots.

Use filtered collections initially: omitting exchange/market filters selects all 14 supported current-market scopes. See each command's effects before running it. Examples here are parser/source-verified; no network or database workflow was executed for this documentation assignment.

items.title: Synchronize the catalogue
items.text:
Synchronization is a network and registry-writing operation. For a small selection:

marketforge markets sync --exchange bybit --market spot --instrument BTCUSDT --testing

For a broader scope, omit --instrument; repeat exchange and market options for subsets:

marketforge markets sync --exchange bybit --exchange okx --market linear --testing

Exchange and market filters select supported combinations, not paired positional tuples. With neither, collection visits all 14 scopes. An unsupported-only selection fails. Independent scope failures do not stop other scopes; inspect the final per-source outcomes.

Provider Spot Linear Inverse Binance Spot Perpetual and dated futures Perpetual and dated futures Bybit Spot Perpetual and dated futures Perpetual and dated futures OKX Spot SWAP and FUTURES SWAP and FUTURES Gate.io Spot Perpetual and delivery Perpetual only Bitget Spot Perpetual and delivery when listed Not collected

Options are excluded from current markets collection. A dated-contract parser does not guarantee a currently listed contract. Expired/historical records remain stored; current endpoints do not establish an exhaustive expired-contract catalogue. Absence from sync does not automatically delete or delist a retained record.

items.title: Browse without network access
items.text:
marketforge markets list --testing --exchange bybit --market spot --limit 20
marketforge markets list --testing --base-asset ETH --quote-asset USDT --match 'ETH*'
marketforge --json markets list --testing --exchange okx --market inverse
marketforge markets show bybit.spot.BTCUSDT --testing

Asset filters are exact and case-insensitive. --instrument matches an exact native symbol; --match is a case-insensitive full-symbol glob supporting * and ?, not regular expressions. Quote it in the shell. %, _ and bracket expressions are literal. Filters combine with AND. The list default is 50 rows, bounded to 1–10000; JSON lists obey the limit and report truncation.

items.title: Identity and contract details
items.text:
Market category (spot, linear, inverse) and instrument type (spot, perpetual, future) are distinct. Use the reference returned by list, ordinarily exchange.market.symbol. When types collide on the same native symbol, use exchange.market.instrument_type.symbol; an ambiguous short reference fails. Do not derive identity by splitting symbols or guessing a date suffix. A policy's explicit instrument references must match the catalogue's canonical returned references.

show groups identity, native status, launch/expiry when supplied, assets/settlement, tick size, quantity step and constraints, quantity denomination, and contract value/unit. Missing specifications stay missing. Expiry is supplied for dated futures, not fabricated from perpetual placeholder timestamps. Retained inactive/expired entries can still appear in browsing; they are not a promise that refresh will collect them.

Next, retrieve current statistics for the successfully synchronized selection. A symbol-filtered sync certifies that selection; it is not a full-scope sync for an unfiltered refresh.

See the unified Forge workflow for managed builds, manually authored profiles, historical registration declarations, namespace mappings and dataset-registration recovery.

items.title: Historical authority during initialization
items.text: mf init --testing now appends historical specification and family evidence after catalogue synchronization, before ranking publication. Existing downloaded bytes remain in place. See historical inference policy for evidence precedence, BTC reference constraints, provenance, incomplete family populations, cached archive discovery and options limitations. Initialization reports metadata readiness separately from exchange collection failures.

items.title: Refresh a synchronized selection
items.text:
After a successful matching metadata sync, refresh statistics:

marketforge markets refresh --exchange bybit --market spot --instrument BTCUSDT --testing
marketforge markets show bybit.spot.BTCUSDT --testing

Refresh contacts public endpoints and writes retained observations. Browsing reads stored values only. A current successful metadata membership is required for each selected scope; older or incomplete syncs do not certify the universe. A broad successful sync can support a symbol-filtered refresh; a narrow sync does not certify an unfiltered refresh. Refresh does not automatically synchronize metadata.

A scope's browsing cache is published only when its required endpoint sequence succeeds. Individual observations can be retained before a later failure, so a failed scope may leave diagnostic observations without updating the displayed latest values. Successful independent scopes remain usable when others fail. Read collection status and per-scope outcomes rather than assuming every value was refreshed.

items.title: What values mean
items.text:
Value Meaning and availability Last price Native quote units per base unit, when supplied; not an execution guarantee or separate time series. Base/quote volume Rolling quantities in their stated asset; fields differ by provider and derivative type. Missing is not zero. Contract volume Contract count where mapped. Convert only using the applicable saved contract specification. Turnover Native monetary activity in the recorded denomination; may be reported, contract-value derived, or an explicitly flagged volume/last-price estimate. Open interest Optional current quantity with its explicit unit (base, quote or contracts); not comparable across units by bare number. Funding rate Optional signed raw rate when returned; not annualized or converted to a universal funding interval. Dated futures have no funding value.

Spot does not universally expose funding/open interest. The mapper retains Bybit open interest in base units for linear and quote units for inverse, Gate derivative open interest in contracts, and available Bitget open interest in base units. Binance/OKX ticker mapping does not retrieve additional funding or open-interest endpoints. A field supported by the model need not be populated for every source.

items.title: Provider-specific volume and turnover
items.text:
Mapping Monetary interpretation Binance spot/linear Reported quoteVolume; volume is base volume. Binance inverse Native quote turnover if supplied; otherwise contract count × verified quote-denominated contract value. baseVolume remains base quantity. Bybit spot/linear turnover24h in quote; volume24h in base. Bybit inverse volume24h supplies quote turnover; turnover24h supplies base quantity. Do not treat the former as contract count. OKX spot volCcy24h quote quantity and vol24h base quantity. OKX inverse Contract vol24h × verified quote face value. OKX linear volCcy24h base quantity × last, explicitly estimated; not accumulated execution-time monetary turnover. Gate.io Reported spot quote_volume or derivative volume_24h_quote; available base/contract quantities remain separate. Bitget Ordinary products use turnover24h; Reality spot products use platform-local platformTurnover24h.

Bitget Reality classification uses metadata isReality, not an R prefix. Broader turnover and volume are not substituted for missing platform-local data. Reality base volume remains missing rather than dividing turnover by last price. Unknown spot classification or incompatible legacy observations need metadata/statistics refresh, not guessed units. Raw values and interpretation evidence are retained.

USDT, USDC and USD are distinct. A contract's settlement currency alone does not establish turnover denomination. Reported native money is not multiplied by face value again. See rankings for explicit currency conversion and estimate controls.

items.title: Timestamps and freshness
items.text:
fetched_at is retrieval time. source_observed_at is the upstream ticker time when supplied. window_start, window_end and window_basis describe the statistic's interval, not the timestamp of every underlying trade.

Binance's supplied openTime/closeTime are retained. OKX/Bitget ticker generation timestamps support inferred preceding 24-hour windows. Without source time, the window is inferred from fetch time and labeled accordingly. A separate last-trade price timestamp is not invented: conversion evidence identifies the ticker/fetch-time proxy.

Stored browsing marks missing collection separately from freshness; stale is based on fetched_at older than one hour (or absent). This display rule is weaker than ranking freshness: ranking checks fetch time and source-window time, future timestamps, and inter-window alignment. Re-fetching an old source interval does not make it suitable for ranking.

These are retained current/rolling observations, not historical tick data or a backtest-ready point-in-time dataset.

items.title: Filter, sort and inspect
items.text:
marketforge markets list --testing --exchange okx --market linear --sort turnover --limit 30
marketforge markets list --testing --base-asset ETH --sort freshness --limit 20
marketforge --json markets show bybit.spot.BTCUSDT --testing

identity is the default sort. turnover sorts descending within native denomination groups, never by a hidden cross-currency conversion. freshness orders by stored measured/window-end time, not the one-hour fetch-time indicator. There is no --instrument-type option on markets list; use returned type metadata, exact symbols or qualified show references.

For stale/missing results, inspect the last collection's per-scope errors, synchronize changed metadata if necessary, and deliberately refresh the required scope. Do not convert missing values into zeros or loosen policy constraints without understanding the resulting comparison.

items.title: Build and inspect market rankings
items.text: Rankings publish an immutable view of eligible retained observations under a named TOML policy. They describe measured activity, not trading signals. Changing current statistics or a policy does not rewrite an existing snapshot.

items.title: Choose the comparison
items.text:
Turnover (metric = "turnover_24h") compares monetary activity in one explicit currency. Optional stored spot prices value aggregate native turnover at reference prices; this is not reconstruction of FX at each trade. Derivative last prices are not conversion sources. USD/USDT/USDC equivalence is never automatic.

Volume (metric = "volume") compares base-asset quantities within each base asset. ETH quantities can share an ETH group across spot, perpetuals and futures; BTC has a different group and its own rank 1. Unique storage position is not a global cross-asset score; group_rank is the within-asset rank. See the complete policies.

items.title: Create and publish a policy
items.text:
new writes a strict version-2 turnover template, without opening an editor:

marketforge markets rank new activity

Edit data/.config/markets/rankings/activity.toml manually to select your universe, comparison, and intended partial-coverage behavior. Validate it before publication:

marketforge markets rank validate activity
marketforge markets rank build activity --testing
marketforge markets rank list --testing
marketforge markets rank show activity --testing --limit 30

build performs no network refresh; it reads retained observations and writes a published snapshot. A successful matching sync and fresh statistics are prerequisites. It evaluates the full selected universe, not the display limit. Explicit instrument references must exist in the selected catalogue; eligible spot conversion prices can be outside the ranking subset but must already be stored.

By default a policy is strict: stale, missing, estimated-disallowed, incompatible-window or unconvertible inputs reject publication. allow_partial_universe = true explicitly permits exclusions and partial-refresh inputs; it does not make missing values valid or disable age/unit checks. At least one included entry is still required. Failed builds roll back their publication; older published snapshots remain available.

items.title: Inspect a pinned result
items.text:
marketforge markets rank show activity --testing --excluded --all
marketforge markets rank show activity --testing --instrument-type perpetual --quote-asset USDT
marketforge --json markets rank show activity --testing

A name resolves the latest published snapshot by creation time then UUID. Use a returned SNAPSHOT_UUID to pin one publication; replace that placeholder in commands. Name resolution applies no age/partial-universe cutoff, so inspect creation time and coverage rather than assuming latest means fresh.

marketforge markets rank show SNAPSHOT_UUID --testing --conversion 1
marketforge markets rank show SNAPSHOT_UUID --testing --base-asset ETH --match 'ETH*'

--conversion accepts a stored full instrument reference or unique storage position. It exposes native amount, rate, path, timestamps and source observations; volume snapshots expose derivation evidence. Human show defaults to 50 included rows and grouped exclusion reasons; --excluded adds excluded rows and --all removes row limits. JSON always returns all matching entries and evidence, regardless of human row limit. Filters preserve original positions/group ranks and do not rebuild the snapshot.

items.title: Conversion and volume evidence
items.text:
Turnover conversion precedence is identity, explicit manual rate, explicit equivalence, then eligible stored spot prices. Automatic paths use one pair or one bridge, without mixed-exchange legs. Same-exchange paths take priority; cross-exchange paths require permission. Freshness, future-time, price-leg skew and turnover-window alignment checks apply separately. A stale manual override fails rather than silently falling back to spot prices.

estimates controls volume-derived turnover estimates such as OKX linear quantity × last; converting reported turnover by FX is a separate valuation convention. Manual preferences can move specified turnover instruments ahead of score order; ties otherwise use score then stable reference. Inspect the policy before treating a rank as pure descending activity.

Volume prefers reliable reported base quantity, including zero. A saved base-denominated contract face value permits exact contract-count conversion; quote-denominated face value divided by a matching positive reference price is estimated. Missing specification/scope evidence causes exclusion. Policies exclude estimates by default. Each result retains its formula, inputs, observation and specification evidence.

New snapshots freeze identity and asset metadata. Older snapshots may fall back to retained observation evidence or current catalogue fields; JSON metadata_sources and human warnings identify this. Current-catalogue fallback can change for old entries, while published scores/order remain pinned.

items.title: Update standard policies
items.text:
After a suitable metadata sync and with standard turnover.toml/volume.toml policies already installed:

marketforge markets rank update turnover --testing
marketforge markets rank update --testing

Unlike build, update performs one global statistics refresh, then publishes the named standard policy or both independently, pinned to that refresh. It accepts only turnover and volume, not custom names, and does not create missing policy files or synchronize metadata. A partial refresh/build can produce nonzero status even if one snapshot was published. Inspect each result; no automatic rollback of the other successful publication is implied.

items.title: Troubleshooting and maintenance
items.text:
For missing/stale data, inspect sync membership and scope errors, then intentionally refresh. For missing currency paths, collect suitable spot inputs or configure an explicit justified rule; do not assume a stablecoin peg. For window mismatch, inspect source end times and tolerance: a fresh fetch alone is insufficient. Strict rejection and a partial publication are different outcomes.

markets rank delete previews snapshots by policy, UUID or --all; adding --apply deletes eligible snapshots and owned evidence transactionally after re-resolving the selection. Referenced snapshots remain blocked. This is explicit maintenance, separate from immutability under normal publication. See deletion syntax and effects.
